paper_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: How is the molecular structure of the electron acceptor BS3TSe-4F derived from the previously reported BP4T-4F?
qa_pairs.answer: BS3TSe-4F is designed by regio-selectively replacing two sulfur atoms in the central and lateral positions of the BP4T-4F pi-core with selenium atoms. This pseudosymmetric substitution strategy is intended to maintain the typical molecular packing mode of Y6 derivatives while modifying the electronic properties.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance metrics of the record-breaking ternary organic solar cell based on the D18/BS3TSe-4F:Y6-O system?
qa_pairs.answer: The ternary planar-mixed heterojunction (PMHJ) organic solar cell using D18/BS3TSe-4F:Y6-O (1:0.1 weight ratio) achieved a record power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.03%. This was accompanied by an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.845 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 29.41 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 76.56%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: How does the asymmetric selenium substitution in BS3TSe-4F affect the dielectric constant and exciton binding energy compared to the S9TBO-F acceptor?
qa_pairs.answer: The asymmetric selenium substitution in BS3TSe-4F increases the dielectric constant (εr) of the D18/BS3TSe-4F blend to 2.80, which is significantly higher than the 2.15 observed for the D18/S9TBO-F blend. Consequently, the exciton binding energy of the BS3TSe-4F blend is reduced to 0.381 eV (compared to 0.495 eV for S9TBO-F), which facilitates more efficient exciton dissociation.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Why does the planar-mixed heterojunction (PMHJ) architecture yield higher efficiency than the bulk heterojunction (BHJ) architecture for the D18:BS3TSe-4F system?
qa_pairs.answer: The PMHJ device achieved a PCE of 18.48%, whereas the BHJ device only reached 16.14%. This performance gap is likely due to poor morphological compatibility between the highly crystalline donor (D18) and acceptor (BS3TSe-4F) materials when mixed in a standard BHJ blend, which is mitigated by the PMHJ structure.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What are the optical bandgap and frontier molecular orbital energy levels of the BS3TSe-4F acceptor?
qa_pairs.answer: BS3TSe-4F has a narrow optical bandgap (Eg opt) of 1.280 eV, with an absorption onset extending to 969 nm. Its HOMO energy level is -5.60 eV and its LUMO energy level is -3.86 eV.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: According to DFT calculations, how does the molecular asymmetry of BS3TSe-4F influence charge generation compared to the symmetric S9TBO-F?
qa_pairs.answer: DFT calculations show that the pseudosymmetric BS3TSe-4F has a stronger tendency to generate free charge carriers because its molecular asymmetry reduces electron-hole overlapping in certain dimer packing patterns. For example, the electron-hole overlapping in Dimer D2 is minimized to 0.241.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: How does the radiative recombination loss of BS3TSe-4F-based devices compare to S9TBO-F-based devices?
qa_pairs.answer: BS3TSe-4F-based devices exhibit a lower radiative recombination loss (ΔE2) of 0.053 eV, compared to 0.062 eV for S9TBO-F-based devices. This lower radiative loss helps compensate for other energy losses, leading to an overall lower energy loss (Eloss) in the BS3TSe-4F derived device.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIWAXS characterization, what are the molecular orientation and coherence lengths (CLs) of the D18/BS3TSe-4F films?
qa_pairs.answer: GIWAXS characterization indicates that D18/BS3TSe-4F films possess a 'face-on' orientation. The coherence lengths (CLs) are 77 Å in the in-plane (IP) direction and 20.4 Å in the out-of-plane (OoP) direction.
qa_pairs.source_title: Achieving 19% Power Conversion Efficiency in Planar-Mixed Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells Using a Pseudosymmetric Electron Acceptor
